_about: Public-domain George Putnam (1807-1878), Unitarian minister of the First Religious Society in Roxbury, Massachusetts, for the Word Hoard: his discourse on the death of President Harrison, Spiritual Renewal, Remarks upon Sumner's oration, the 1846 election sermon, God and our Country, a Roxbury memorial address, a Harvard funeral address (1864), and Sermons preached in Roxbury (1878). Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 95 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

gputnam-harrison: A discourse, on the occasion of the death of William Henry Harrison, ninth president of the United States : delivered at Roxbury, April 16th, 1841 (Boston : W. Crosby and Co., 1841)
gputnam-spiritual-renewal: Spiritual renewal the great work of the Christian Church and ministry : a sermon delivered at the ordination of Rev. Frederic D. Huntington, as pastor of the South Congregational Church in Boston, October 19, 1842 (Boston : William Crosby, 1842)
gputnam-election-1846: A sermon delivered before His Excellency George N. Briggs, governor, His Honor John Reed, lieutenant governor, the honorable Council (Boston : Dutton and Wentworth, printers to the state, 1846)
gputnam-god-and-country: God and our country : a discourse delivered in the First Congregational Church in Roxbury, on Fast Day, April 8, 1847 (catalogued 1847)
gputnam-roxbury-address: An address, delivered before the city government and citizens of Roxbury, on the life and character of the late Henry A. S. Dearborn, mayor of the city. September 3d, 1851 (Roxbury : Norfolk county journal press, 1851)
gputnam-funeral-1864: An address spoken in the college chapel, Cambridge, October 28, 1864, at the funeral of Brig.-Gen ([Boston?, 1864)
gputnam-sermons: Sermons preached in the church of the first religious society in Roxbury (catalogued 1878)
